scenarios.title: Safety setup for ALL native scenarios: use only newly created run-owned profile_<32hex> partitions, never shared Default; QUIRKY_HOME/HOME alone do not prove native storage isolation. Open a browser pane with that explicit UUID profile and verify sandboxed WebKit without Chrome; switch/hide destroys it and return recreates one retained-URL view; resize and overlays stay aligned
In the run-owned UUID profile only, Native address, Back/Forward/Reload/Stop, same-document navigation and Find previous/next/count/close change the actual embedded page and reflect real state
In the run-owned UUID profile only, native zoom applies real WebKit page zoom for half-step levels and reset; viewport menu and native geometry stay coherent when resized and shown again

In the run-owned UUID profile only, opening an owned local HTML fixture displays its native page; Open source file opens that exact canonical in-worktree file and outside-worktree source actions fail visibly

In a run-owned UUID profile only, native guest starts about:blank until supported host claim installs deny-all-then-allow policy. HTTP/HTTPS/file/about:blank work; views://, appdata://, javascript: and data: cannot navigate or invoke shell/daemon RPC. Suggestions, menus, palette and dialogs remain clickable above native content using masks, not only z-index

Two NEW run-owned UUID profile partitions never share site storage; switch preserves pane/tab/URL but recreates guest. Clear must reject completion-unavailable BEFORE any real Session invocation and preserve existing site storage; never clear shared Default without a proven native-root override. App-shell partition/malformed IDs reject. Actual completed native clearing belongs to the queued completion-capability follow-up

In a NEW run-owned UUID profile, click inside native guest content, then verify Cmd+L focuses the host address bar, Cmd+F opens host find, Cmd+R reloads the guest (not the app), Back/Forward and zoom chords target the browser; after focusing another terminal/editor these browser shortcuts no longer intercept its input

While typing in a real terminal pane, agent browser input and Watch updates never steal macOS window or typing focus; browser-specific shortcuts do not override terminal/editor bindings outside browser focus
